newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Ex-HK to Europe rates rise for second time in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Ex-HK to Europe rates rise for second time in Oct.

text.p: Airlines flying cargo from Hong Kong to Europe have introduced their second rate rise within three weeks, Emirates Airlines cargo manager, Jacky Lau said.
The HK50 cents a kg rise was introduced immediately after an informal meeting of carriers yesterday, he told Reuters
Industry sources blamed the latest rise on increasing costs and fuel price hikes, but is less than the HK$2 a kg originally planned.

Ex-Hong Kong to Europe rates have been under pressure for some time.They were being raised on August 1 by HK$3 a kg, by HK$2 a kg on October 1 with a warning they would be increased by a similar amount again on October 10 by a further HK$2 a kg.
But that rise was postponed until a further meeting was held among airline representatives, the source said.

Other carriers at the meeting included Deutsche Lufthansa, AG, China Airlines 2, Singapore Airlines, Martinair, Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and its subsidiary AHK Air Hong Kong Ltd as well as Thai Airways International Ltd and Swissair, Lau added.
The sources said that despite strong demand for cargo space, some carrers uneasy about market reaction to another rise so soon after October 1 and pressured for a reduced increase.
"I believe the market can sustain this rise which is not as substantial as a two dollar rise. I think it will be successful in trying to offset higher operating costs," Lau said.
But Sam Chung, the chairman of the Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents and director and general manager of Fritz Air Freight (HK) Ltd, said he does not think another rise is justified.

"The airlines have already raised their prices so much in such a short time which is not fair for the forwarders. The airlines can put their prices up immediately but the forwarders cannot do that, which means they suffer the loss," Chung said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
